cohort: Births in the US from the CDC's Birth Data files for 2006 (n=4,273,225), with 183,323 meeting inclusion criteria (fetal presentation and ECV status)
finding: Compared to breech controls without attempted ECV, failed ECV was associated with an increased risk of adverse perinatal and obstetrical outcomes.
mod_finding: This study found that compared to breech births without an attempted external cephalic version, failed ECV was associated with increased odds of elective cesarean delivery and cesarean delivery in labor.
